answer: Each epoch the protocol posts U, unestablished keys already accepted this window. An unestablished submit locks one extra unit of this epoch's per-head payout onto every key already in that set and onto the joiner, struck at close. One fake pays 1; the tenth re-taxes ten keys, so the next head costs more (triangle n(n+1)/2). Split keys cannot reset U or spare the ones already seated. The join is the bridge that re-taxes the cohort; a yarrow of aliases still hits every prior fake. A new walnut cannot mint an exemption. No lock, no land.
